levels.title: Understand
levels.subtitle: Use AI to Read, Not Write
levels.move_on_when: You can tell confident-correct from confident-guessing AI without checking every claim.

tasks.title: Tool Setup Guide
tasks.desc: Install Claude Code (and iTerm 2 on macOS). After this you can install everything else by pasting prompts into Claude Code. Plan ~10 minutes for the manual bootstrap, then come back here.

tasks.title: How We Work With AI at Solvd
tasks.desc: Five-minute orientation: why AI fails the way it does, the four principles we use at Solvd, and when to use which tool. This is the entry point — everything else builds on it.

tasks.title: The AI Mindset — 4-property framework
tasks.desc: The diagnostic doc. Next Token Prediction, Knowledge, Working Memory, Steerability. Every success and every failure traces to one of these four — once you internalize them, every later guideline makes sense. Re-read whenever AI surprises you.

tasks.title: Claude Code — Best Practices (Reference)
tasks.desc: Keep this open in a tab. Modes, slash commands, @-references, MCP, custom commands. You won't need every section at Level 1 — skim it now, return to specific sections as you hit them in later levels.

tasks.title: Ask AI to explain code you already know
tasks.desc: Open a project you know well. Use @-references. Ask AI to walk you through the logic. The point is to build a baseline for spotting hallucinations.

tasks.title: Use /btw for side questions
tasks.desc: Try the /btw command mid-task to get quick factual answers without interrupting your flow.

tasks.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT — Andrej Karpathy
tasks.desc: Andrej Karpathy's ~3.5-hour lecture on how LLMs are actually built and how to think about their outputs. The single best non-Anthropic source for mechanical intuition — pretraining, post-training, hallucinations, why models are good at some things and bad at others. Watch before the Anthropic Academy courses below; they assume this kind of mental model.

tasks.title: Claude 101
tasks.desc: Anthropic Academy intro to Claude. Use Claude for routine professional tasks; survey of essential capabilities; signposts to deeper material. Free with certificate.

tasks.title: Claude Code 101
tasks.desc: Anthropic Academy intro to Claude Code (the CLI/IDE coding agent). Installation, writing prompts, workflow management, day-to-day customization. Free with certificate.

tasks.title: Introduction to Claude Cowork
tasks.desc: Working alongside Claude on real files and projects. Covers the task loop, plugins, skills setup, and responsibly steering multi-step work. Free with certificate.

tasks.title: AI Capabilities and Limitations
tasks.desc: How modern generative AI systems work and behave. Identifies types of unexpected outputs (hallucinations, refusals) and applies targeted fixes based on the four machine properties — Next Token Prediction, Knowledge, Working Memory, Steerability. Video-first companion to the 'AI Mindset' reading.

tasks.title: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations
tasks.desc: Anthropic's foundational course on Anthropic Academy — free with certificate. Teaches practical skills for effective, efficient, ethical, and safe AI interaction. Covers the 4-property framework from the 'AI Mindset' reading in depth.

tasks.title: Spot confident-correct vs confident-guessing AI
tasks.desc: You've caught AI hallucinating a few times and know what that looks like.

levels.title: Edit with Review
levels.subtitle: Quality Is the Point — the target level for most engineers at Solvd
levels.move_on_when: You instinctively review diffs, can look at AI-generated code and say 'this is overcomplicated, simplify' and get a better result.

tasks.title: Prompt Patterns
tasks.desc: Effective prompts are short, concrete, verifiable. Covers proven prompt patterns (Socratic, 3x3, Evaluator-Optimizer) and workflow patterns (chaining, parallelization). Read before the 'weak vs strong prompts' practice — it's the toolkit that practice draws on.

tasks.title: Context Engineering
tasks.desc: What AI sees, when, and how. Three context layers (project memory, rules, conversation), automating context injection with hooks, cross-session persistence. The Working Memory property from L1 made operational.

tasks.title: Code Review with AI
tasks.desc: First-pass review framework: Logic → Security → Performance → Maintainability → Style. AI catches patterns; humans validate architecture and business logic. Surgical-changes principle: every changed line traces to the request. Underpins the diff-review-habit practice below.

tasks.title: Debugging with AI
tasks.desc: Give AI the full error context (message, stack, code, what you tried). Use AI for hypothesis generation, never for unverified fixes — AI generates plausible hypotheses, not verified ones. Underpins the 3-try-rule practice below.

tasks.title: Practice weak vs strong prompts
tasks.desc: Pick a task you'd normally prompt vaguely. Rewrite the prompt with explicit constraints. Compare results.

tasks.title: Internalize the diff-review habit
tasks.desc: For one week, read every diff before accepting. Note one thing you caught that you would have missed.

tasks.title: Practice the 3-try rule
tasks.desc: When AI doesn't get it right in 3 attempts, the problem is your prompt or context. Reframe instead of retrying.

tasks.title: Claude Code in Action
tasks.desc: Modes, context control, and the habits that make daily AI usage productive. Free with certificate. Pairs directly with the Prompt Patterns and Code Review with AI readings — the readings provide the principles, the course shows them in motion.

tasks.title: I instinctively review diffs and ask for simplification
tasks.desc: You no longer accept the first output without reading it.

levels.title: Plan and Implement
levels.subtitle: Think Before Building
levels.move_on_when: You never start multi-file work without Plan mode.

tasks.title: Spec-Driven Development
tasks.desc: Write a specification before writing code. Use AI to draft the spec, then generate architecture, then implement step-by-step with explicit STOP points. This is the workflow the 3-step practice below operationalizes — read this first so 'Context → Plan → Implement' has weight behind each word.

tasks.title: AI Model Selection Guide
tasks.desc: Opus for architecture and complex reasoning, Sonnet for daily coding, Haiku for quick queries. L3 is where this first matters — Plan mode and thinking mode let you spend more compute, and choosing the right model for the plan phase vs the code phase is a real productivity lever.

tasks.title: Use the 3-step workflow (Context → Plan → Implement) on a real change
tasks.desc: Pick a real multi-file change you'd otherwise dive straight into. Do all three steps explicitly. Step 1 — Context: @-reference the relevant files and ask AI to analyze the current behavior; no changes yet. Step 2 — Plan: open Plan mode (/plan, or Shift+Tab twice) and describe the desired outcome; read the plan critically and push back before approving. Step 3 — Implement: only after the plan looks right, say 'execute'. The point isn't to do it once — it's to feel the difference between this and 'just ask AI to fix it'. Done when you've shipped one change end-to-end this way and can name one thing the plan caught that you would otherwise have missed.

tasks.title: Use /branch to compare two approaches
tasks.desc: Fork your session. Try approach A and B. Pick the better one.

tasks.title: Claude Code in Action — Plan Mode chapters
tasks.desc: Same Anthropic Academy course as the Level 2 Claude Code in Action — focus this time on the Plan Mode and three-step-workflow chapters. If you already completed the course at Level 2, just rewatch those sections.

tasks.title: I never start >3-file work without a plan

levels.title: Orchestrate
levels.subtitle: Multiply Your Output
levels.move_on_when: You have automated feedback loops; team has shared custom commands.

tasks.title: Creating Claude Code Skills and Plugins
tasks.desc: A skill is a packaged set of instructions, references, and assets that teaches Claude Code domain-specific knowledge. Once installed, it activates automatically when relevant — so anyone on the team gets consistent output without re-explaining the rules. Covers the generic workflow: prompt structure, packaging, local marketplace install, team distribution. This is the foundation for the kind of automation that defines Level 4.

tasks.title: MCP — Model Context Protocol Configuration
tasks.desc: Configure MCP servers in `.mcp.json` to give Claude Code real-time access to documentation, issue trackers, and design tools — replacing stale training data with live context. The way you wire 'AI knows about our Jira / our Figma / our Confluence' without copy-pasting screenshots.

tasks.title: AI Security Policy
tasks.desc: Never put secrets, API keys, passwords, or PII in prompts, CLAUDE.md, or AI rules. Use placeholders for sensitive data. Set up permissions to deny destructive operations. Especially important at Level 4: you're now wiring hooks that auto-execute scripts — security mindset is the guardrail.

tasks.title: Repo Preparation — Making Your Codebase AI-Ready
tasks.desc: Step-by-step guide to preparing any existing codebase for effective AI agent collaboration. The bottleneck usually isn't the model — it's the codebase and environment it works in. Read the overview; follow links into the 10 specific guides (linters, type safety, CI/CD, hooks) as your codebase needs them.

tasks.title: Add a PostToolUse hook for type-checking
tasks.desc: Catch type errors automatically after every edit.

tasks.title: Create a team /review custom command
tasks.desc: Codify your team's review checklist.

tasks.title: Introduction to agent skills
tasks.desc: Anthropic Academy course on building, configuring, and sharing reusable Skills in Claude Code that automatically apply to relevant tasks. The video companion to the Creating Skills and Plugins reading. Free with certificate.

tasks.title: Introduction to subagents
tasks.desc: Anthropic Academy course on Claude Code's sub-agents feature: delegate tasks to isolated assistants, manage context windows efficiently, build specialized workflows while keeping the main conversation focused. The orchestration multiplier — once you can fan work out across subagents, big migrations and audits become feasible. Free with certificate.

tasks.title: I have an automated feedback loop catching bugs

levels.title: AI as Architecture Partner
levels.subtitle: Use AI for thinking, not just doing
levels.move_on_when: There is no Level 6 — you are using AI to challenge your own assumptions.

tasks.title: Recommended AI Tool Stack
tasks.desc: Claude Code is the primary AI coding tool at Solvd; Codex, Cursor, and Copilot are supported alternatives. Every project should be configured with CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md for Codex), rules, MCP servers, and permissions. At Level 5 you're making cross-team tool decisions — this is the stance you're operating from.

tasks.title: Run anti-sycophancy prompting on a real decision
Building with the Claude API
tasks.desc: Comprehensive Anthropic Academy course on working with Anthropic models via the Claude API. Where you stop being a Claude Code user and start being an engineer who builds AI-powered systems. Free with certificate.

tasks.title: Introduction to Model Context Protocol
tasks.desc: Build MCP servers and clients in Python. Master the three MCP primitives — tools, resources, and prompts — to connect Claude with external services. Companion course to the L4 MCP Configuration reading: that one is consumer-side, this one is server-side.

tasks.title: Model Context Protocol: Advanced Topics
tasks.desc: Advanced MCP implementation patterns: sampling, notifications, file-system access, transport mechanisms. Take this after Introduction to MCP when you're ready to ship a production MCP server.
